The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
papers.abstract: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.

papers.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant Γ_{1,4} = 8
papers.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants Γ_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: DistFlow and Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, and Hybrid Exactness via Graph Decomposition
papers.abstract: Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
papers.abstract: We compare the maximum points \(P_Ω\) and \(Q_Ω\) of the torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness, strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity \[ \sup_Ω \frac{|P_Ω-Q_Ω|}{\operatorname{diam}(Ω)}=\frac12. \] Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

papers.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
papers.abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.

papers.title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. The investigation focuses on a quantum-enhanced scheme in which squeezing is added to the derivative mode of a Gaussian probe beam as a means of estimating photon-beam displacement. The performance of the scheme is compared against the standard quantum limit achieved by an optimal classical beam-displacement estimation scheme under a fair same-total-energy constraint. We find that although the benefit provided by squeezing rapidly diminishes as the inter-satellite distance increases due to diffraction-induced beam spreading and subsequent truncation by the finite receiver aperture, a quantum advantage can still be expected over inter-satellite distances up to approximately 100 km under practical satellite configurations. This distance scale between satellites is anticipated for Starlink-type satellite constellations.

papers.title: Only constant mean curvature surfaces in $E(κ,τ)$, $τ\ne0$, have a holomorphic original Abresch-Rosenberg differential
papers.abstract:
For immersed surfaces in the homogeneous spaces $E(κ,τ)$ with $τ
e0$, we prove that the original Abresch--Rosenberg differential $[2(H+iτ)p-(κ-4τ^2)A^2]\,dζ^2$ is holomorphic if and only if the mean curvature $H$ is constant; here $p\,dζ^2$ is the Hopf differential and $A=\langleξ,\partial_ζangle$. The result is local: no completeness, compactness or analyticity is assumed, and there are no exceptional surfaces. Where $dH

e4τ^2$ the structure equations become a rational system whose solutions are algebraic, and an embedding into a field of Puiseux series excludes every branch. In $M^2(κ)	imes\mathbb{R}$, $κ

We also show that the Hopf-cylinder alternative in a theorem of Dorfmeister, Inoguchi and Kobayashi contains no non-CMC surface.

papers.title: Biorthogonal universal quantum control
papers.abstract: As a paradigm for describing open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation generally modifies state norms, complicating coherent control over the system's Hilbert space. With a general instantaneous frame spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for discrete-variable systems governed by time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of controlled transitionless passages. We further identify the parametric constraints under which the transformation linking the initial and final states becomes unitary. As a result, the final system state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer and a holomonic quantum gate implemented by a non-Hermitian three-level system in $Λ$ type. For the population transfer, controlled gain and loss reduce the required coherent pulse area, enabling shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark with the same average Rabi frequency. Our work integrates the universal quantum control (UQC) into the biorthogonal representation, displaying full-rank passage engineering with coherent operations in non-Hermitian systems.

papers.title: Anomalous superradiant phases in a quantum Rabi zigzag chain under a synthetic gauge field
papers.abstract: We present the phase diagram of a one-dimensional quantum Rabi zigzag chain under an artificial gauge field, which is implemented via phase-modulated next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping. For a system size of $N=8$, we analytically determine the order parameters and critical thresholds, identifying five distinct superradiant phases. For strong nearest-neighbor (NN) coupling, the system exhibits either a ferro-superradiant (FSR) or an antiferro-superradiant (AFSR) phase depending on its sign. Increasing NNN coupling induces a stripe antiferro-superradiant (sAFSR) phase with antiparallel NNN and parallel NN displacements, which is distinct from the conventional AFSR phase. Tuning the magnetic flux drives the system into chiral or antichiral superradiant phases with opposite ground-state photon currents, which are different from the conventional superradiant phases. Remarkably, geometric frustration within each triangular plaquette stabilizes chiral phases even at small magnetic flux while suppressing the sAFSR phase, which vanishes for $N=6$. Mapping the system onto an effective magnetic Hamiltonian yields an analogous phase diagram featuring distinct magnetic phases, offering insight into the anomalous superradiant phases. This equivalence establishes a quantum optical platform for simulating chiral magnetism.

papers.title: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing
papers.abstract: Determining whether every trajectory of the linear system $\dot{x}=Ax$ converges to zero (or, equivalently, whether $A$ is Hurwitz stable) is a fundamental problem in control theory. It arises, for example, in verifying the stability of feedback controllers and state observers, as well as of linearized dynamical models. We study the quantum query complexity of deciding whether a matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ is Hurwitz stable, given an exact normalized block-encoding of $A$. The query complexity is characterized in terms of the system dimension $n$ and a supplied lower bound $0<ν\leq ω_A$ on the imaginary-axis distance $ω_A:=\min_{t\in\mathbb{R}}σ_{\min}(A-\mathrm{i}tI)$, where $σ_{\min}(A)$ is the smallest singular value of $A$. We prove a query-complexity lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{n}/ν)$, which holds even when $A$ is restricted to be real and diagonal. For general matrices with nonzero $ω_A$, we encode an approximation of the right-half-plane spectral projector $\operatorname{sign}^+(A):=(I+\operatorname{sign}(A))/2$ as a block of a matrix inverse, where $A$ is Hurwitz if and only if the projector is zero. To test this, we produce a quantum algorithm which determines if a $(β,b,1/(4\sqrt{n}))$-block-encoded projector matrix (like $\operatorname{sign}^+(A)$) is zero or not; for constant success probability, it has complexity $Θ(β\sqrt{n})$. When the zero test is applied to specific approximations of $\operatorname{sign}^+(A)$, this yields an upper bound of $O(\sqrt{n}ν^{-2}\log(\sqrt{n}/ν))$ queries in the general case, and $O(\sqrt{n}ν^{-1}\log n)$ when $A$ is Hermitian or normal. The latter upper bound matches the lower bound up to a logarithmic factor. Thus the dimension dependence of quantum Hurwitz testing is nearly optimal, while the remaining factor in the non-normal case isolates an open conditioning gap.

papers.title: General Frequency Principle for Linear Approximation Classes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a general frequency principle under gradient descent training for the finite linear approximation classes. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the learner amplitude relative to the target amplitude vanishes at high frequencies, uniformly throughout training. We also establish sufficient conditions for low-frequency priority, covering single-frequency targets trained separately and two frequency components trained in the same run. This general frequency principle does not imply that lower frequencies always converge faster. Instead, for two frequencies that satisfy certain comparison conditions, one component will take longer to learn than the other; and in common cases, the longer component has higher frequency. Numerical experiments with Legendre and trigonometric bases validate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Traveling Salesman Problem on Graphs with Proportional Independent Set
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in undirected graphs with arbitrary real edge costs and an independent set of size at least $αn$, for any fixed $3/7<α\le1/2$. It runs in $O^*(γ(α)^n)$ time for an explicit constant $γ(α)<2$; for bipartite graphs, the bound is $O^*((1+2\sqrt2)^{n/2})\approx O^*(1.957^n)$. The algorithm is based on a restricted Held--Karp dynamic program. Its state enumeration uses structural properties of minimum-cost assignments arising from a regular triangulation of a product of simplices.

papers.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+Δ|\ne\emptyset$, where $Δ$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.

papers.title: Sharp Solyanik Estimates for Discrete and Ergodic Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators
papers.abstract: Let $U_1,\dots,U_n$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space, and let $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(α)$ denote the sharp Tauberian constant of the associated ergodic uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. Hagelstein and Parissis showed that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(α)-1\lesssim_n(1/α-1)^{1/(n(n+1))}$ as $α\to1^-$ and asked whether this exponent is sharp. We prove that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(α)-1\lesssim_n(1/α-1)^{1/n}$ for all such transformations, and that this is sharp: equality of the ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants holds for every action admitting arbitrarily large Rokhlin towers (in particular for every free action, ergodic or not), and the discrete constant satisfies $\widetilde{C}_{\mathrm{HL}}(α)-1\asymp_n(1/α-1)^{1/n}$. For $n\ge2$ the sharp ergodic exponent $1/n$ is strictly smaller than the sharp Euclidean exponent $2/(n+1)$ recently obtained by Mukherjee; the discrepancy is caused by a lattice ``first layer'' effect. We also show that the discrete Tauberian constants of the Hardy--Littlewood and strong maximal operators dominate their Euclidean counterparts; for the strong maximal operator this yields $C^{*}_{\mathrm{S}}=C_{\mathrm{S}}$ for every free action.

papers.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
papers.abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{λ,μ}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_λ(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_μ(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $λ$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{λ,μ}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $λ$ is a hook shape, when $λ$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{λ,μ}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.

papers.title: Dilation systems with two generators and the optimal Riesz bounds of a basis of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: For two $1$-periodic functions $ψ_1,ψ_2\in L^2(0,1)$ with mean zero we characterize when $\{1\}\cup\{ψ_1(α\cdot x),ψ_2(α\cdot x)\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}^d,\,α\succ0}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2([0,1]^d)$, in terms of a $2\times2$ matrix of Dirichlet series, and we compute its optimal bounds. The tool is a $2\times2$ matrix version of the theorem of Hedenmalm, Lindqvist and Seip for systems of dilations with two generators, proved through the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space of the infinite polydisk. In particular, we get the optimal bounds $2/3$ and $3/2$ for $ψ_1,ψ_2$ the triangle waves considered by Daubechies, DeVore, Foucart, Hanin and Petrova in $L^2(0,1)$, and the extended version in $L^2([0,1]^d)$ defined by Schneider and Vybíral.

papers.title: Solyanik Estimates for Ergodic Flows
papers.abstract: Let $\{T_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space $(Ω,Σ,μ)$ and let $T^*$ be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant $C(α)=\sup_{μ(E)>0}\frac{μ(\{T^*χ_E>α\})}{μ(E)}$,$0<α<1$, equals $1/α$ for every $α\in(0,1)$, unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case $C(α)=1$ for every $α$. In particular the Solyanik estimate $\lim_{α\to1^-}C(α)=1$ holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate $C(α)-1\le 1/α-1$ holds with equality. This answers the one-parameter case of a question of Hagelstein and Parissis. The main point is the lower bound, which is obtained from a lacunary cross-section built out of the upcrossings of a probe function along the orbits of the flow.

papers.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

papers.title: Critical Optimizers for the Finite-Rank Fractional Lieb--Thirring Inequality
papers.abstract: We study optimal potentials for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring problem at the eigenvalue-counting endpoint, for \(0<s<1\) and \(d>2s\). Using the zero-energy Birman--Schwinger formulation, we prove a profile decomposition of normalized optimizing sequences with exact splitting of rank and potential mass, and strong approximation in \(L^{d/(2s)}\). Strict subadditivity yields existence and compactness modulo translations and dilations. At rank two, the optimal constant equals the rank-one constant, the supremum is not attained, and every normalized optimizing sequence splits into two Sobolev potentials. We also prove strict increase of the minimal potential masses and a uniform spectral gap for optimizing sequences. For each optimizer, we derive an Euler--Lagrange system and establish boundedness, local Hölder regularity and \(V(x)=|x|^{-4s}(c_\infty+o(1))\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), with \(c_\infty\geq0\). The conformal orbit of every optimizer contains a representative with a strictly positive asymptotic coefficient.

papers.title: Encoded reversible addition in constant Toffoli depth
papers.abstract: We show that reversible in-place quantum addition modulo $2^n-1$ can be implemented in constant Toffoli depth using $O(n)$ space, provided that the variables are encoded in a certain non-standard form. Using measurement-based uncomputation, the Toffoli depth can be reduced to one. We also present space-depth tradeoffs and an application to programmable rotations.

papers.title: Koopman--Lyapunov and Koopman--Riccati Controller Synthesis
papers.abstract: While the Koopman operator-based lifted representations of nonlinear autonomous and controlled systems have been well covered in the literature, the direct controller synthesis problem largely remains open. As the controlled system is generally a bilinear (instead of fully linear) Koopman model, controller synthesis appears to lose the linear--quadratic structures of the classical Lyapunov and Riccati methods for finite-dimensional linear systems. However, in infinite dimensions, bilinearity in the feature map should be merely artifactual and hence reducible to linearity in principle. In this work, by considering the operator semigroups in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space with a linear--Sobolev kernel and utilizing the Yosida approximation of their generators, the synthesis problems of a stabilizing controller and an input-unconstrained optimal controller can be formulated as an operator Lyapunov inequality and an operator Riccati equation, respectively. These formulations recover the desirable linear--quadratic structures, and hence, with sample data, they are solvable efficiently in analogous ways to usual linear systems by semidefinite programming solvers and Kleinman iterations, respectively. In addition to proving control performance bounds dependent on the sampling denseness and Yosida regularization, through numerical comparison to linearized LQR, bilinear EDMD-based synthesis, nonlinear MPC, and Koopman MPC methods on numerical models and process control examples, this work demonstrates the proposed Koopman--Riccati synthesis as a computationally efficient approach to obtain a near-optimal state-feedback control law.

papers.title: Turnpike Properties for Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Indefinite Cost Functionals
papers.abstract: Continuous-time exploratory stochastic control provides a stochastic control framework for the exploration--exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning. In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems as the time horizon $T\to\infty$, and establish so-called turnpike properties for such problems. In the finite-horizon setting, we derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem and analyze its long-time structure. We formulate an exploratory static distribution optimization problem analogous to the classical static optimization problem and identify the corresponding static reference object. We prove a turnpike property for the optimal state process relative to a stochastic reference process, as well as a Wasserstein turnpike property for the optimal control distribution. In addition to the exploratory control formulation, another key feature of our results is that, by introducing a joint coercivity condition, we allow the cost functional to be indefinite and the controlled state system to be merely stabilizable. Consequently, the derived turnpike property is novel even within the classical stochastic LQ control framework.

papers.title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.

papers.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -Δu=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

papers.title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
papers.abstract: Let $A_ρ$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_ρ$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.

papers.title: Strong solvability and its failure for critical SDEs
papers.abstract: We revisit the construction of strong solutions to singular SDEs by compactness on Wiener space. For spatially varying diffusion coefficients, assuming sufficiently small form bounds on the drift and diffusion gradient, we use basic energy estimates and an extended compactness criterion for Wiener functionals to construct an approximation-independent stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. Both forward and inverse maps have local Sobolev moment bounds, and the resulting strong solutions are pathwise unique in a class of solutions satisfying a Krylov estimate. We also show that the endpoint critical condition $b\in L^\infty_tL^d_x$, together with $\mathrm{div } b=0$ does not guarantee the existence of a strong solution. For every $d\geq2$, we construct a SDE with a divergence-free drift in this class and an additive Brownian noise, started from the origin, has a weak solution unique in law, but no strong solution. The proof uses logarithmic rescaling to characterize strong solvability by whether the sample measures of an associated stationary diffusion are Dirac masses. Positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent, combined with random SRB theory, rules out this concentration and hence strong solvability.

papers.title: Bounds for lattice points in terms of volume and successive minima
papers.abstract: We prove, in every dimension, the upper bound conjectured by Betke, Henk and Wills for the lattice-point enumerator in terms of volume and successive minima. For every convex body $K\subset R^n$ and full-rank lattice $Λ$, we establish $$ \#(K\capΛ)\le\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\detΛ}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1+\frac{iλ_i}{2}\right), $$ where $λ_i$ are the successive minima of $(K-K)/2$ with respect to $Λ$. Equality holds precisely for lattice translates of positive integral dilates of unimodular simplices. We also prove $$ \#(\mathrm{int}K\capΛ)\ge\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\detΛ} \left(1-\frac{n}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}λ_i-\frac{n}{2}λ_n\right), $$ which implies the lower estimate with factor $1-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n iλ_i$. In dimension two we prove the lower bound with factor $(1-λ_1/2)(1-λ_2)$ when $λ_2\le1$. We also observe that a conjectured product lower bound for origin-symmetric bodies fails in dimension three. The proofs combine geometric compression, lattice-cell counts in coordinate sections, and an elementary coefficient comparison.

papers.title: Circular regular dessins with underlying graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$: the metacyclic case
papers.abstract: A dessin is a 2-cell embedding of a connected bipartite graph into an orientable closed surface. It is regular if the colour- and orientation-preserving automorphism group acts regularly on edges, and circular if every face boundary is a simple cycle. We classify and enumerate circular regular dessins of the complete bipartite multigraph ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$ ($e\ge f\ge 2$, $d\ge 1$) whose automorphism group is {\it metacyclic}. This extends the work of Fan (circular, metacyclic) and Cai--Hu (regular, metacyclic) from simple graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}$ to multigraphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$. Such dessins correspond to non-exact bicyclic factorisations $G=ła\rłb\r\cong\ZZ_{2^{e+d}}\ZZ_{2^{f+d}}$, where $ła\r\capłb\r\cong\ZZ_{2^d}$ and $łba\r\cap ła\r=łba\r\cap łb\r=1$. In general, a group admitting such a factorisation need not be metacyclic; in this paper we impose the additional condition that $G$ is a metacyclic 2-group. Under this assumption, we obtain explicit enumeration formulas for the number of such dessins up to isomorphism. Together with the known classifications for simple graphs (the case $d=0$), this completes the enumeration of the metacyclic case for 2-power complete bipartite multigraphs.

papers.title: Entangled Measurement Outcomes for Optimal Postselection in Quantum Batteries
papers.abstract: Postselection can enhance the performance of a selected quantum battery branch, raising the question of whether the optimum can always be achieved by product measurements on the auxiliary subsystems. For battery auxiliary states obtained by mixing a pure state with global white noise of strength p, the conditional ergotropy reduces to a generalized Rayleigh quotient. For 0<p<1, product postselection attains the joint optimum if and only if the eigenspace associated with the largest generalized eigenvalue contains a product vector. For two auxiliary qubits, a strict product-joint gap therefore occurs precisely when this eigenspace is one dimensional and spanned by an entangled vector. Noisy W and GHZ states display qualitatively different behavior: the three qubit W state exhibits a strict gap throughout 0<p<1, whereas the three qubit GHZ state admits a product optimum. For interacting two qubit batteries, the optimal postselection can switch from a Bell outcome to a product outcome as the coupling strength is varied. By contrast, the outcome averaged capacity and ergotropy are independent of the measurement basis, showing that the joint measurement advantage is genuinely postselective.

papers.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
papers.abstract: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations. Finding solutions to this problem requires an exponential number of operations, hindering the ability of exact solvers to deal with large instances, which must therefore be tackled using heuristics, often leading to suboptimal results. Quantum-based algorithms may allow us to find exact solutions in polynomial time with high probability, offering a potential future alternative to classical solvers and in this work, we focus on the QAOA. Our novel contributions are a parameter-initialization strategy that improves the convergence probability and the integration of the subtour constraints directly into the optimization without using additional qubits by employing an approximation of exponential equality constraints. We believe that our results pave the way for effectively solving instances of VRP using quantum-based solutions, leveraging the space-efficient problem encoding and our initialization strategy, which limits the effect of barren-plateau under random parameter initialization.

papers.title: Derived products and top-degree inverse limits
papers.abstract: We compute top derived products and inverse limits on products of affine lines with doubled origin over $B[s]$, for any nonzero commutative ring $B$. For every $B$-module $M$, the two top obstruction modules fit into an explicit exact sequence and contain $M^{\mathbb N}/M^{(\mathbb N)}$as a natural $B$-module direct summand.This gives exact product dimensions, sharp vanishing bounds for inverse sequences, and faithfulness in the coefficient module. For a Grothendieck category of finite product dimension, we also obtain degree shifts under adjoining commuting locally nilpotent endomorphisms and prove that this construction preserves top-degree vanishing for epimorphic inverse sequences. A fixed Gabriel--Popescu presentation then describes the general top obstruction through actual Ext sequences and separates two module-theoretic terms.

papers.title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
papers.abstract: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Clusters of primes revisited
papers.abstract: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.

papers.title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
papers.abstract: For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$. We prove that for these classes of words, their reconstruction thresholds are bounded by a function of the structural complexity of the class. We also study weak deck reconstruction, in which subwords may contain "wildcard" symbols that map to either 0 or 1. By generalizing a "template lemma" of Dudík and Schulman, we improve the upper bound in an open question about weak reconstruction from Dudík and Schulman. Finally, for the class of periodic words with period $d$, we prove that its in-class reconstruction threshold is equal to the general reconstruction threshold for words of length $d$, and give a general template construction producing further classes with the same threshold-preservation phenomenon.

papers.title: Long-Time Behavior towards Generic Riemann Solutions for Radiative Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We study the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional radiative Euler equations, where the Riemann pattern consists of a $1$-rarefaction wave, a $2$-contact discontinuity, and a $3$-shock wave. We prove that, for sufficiently small wave strengths and initial perturbations, the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution, which converges uniformly as $t\to \infty$ to a composite wave of the $1$-rarefaction wave, $2$-viscous contact wave, and $3$-radiative shock profile with a time-dependent shift. As a key ingredient, we establish a comprehensive set of quantitative estimates for weak radiative shock profiles. Our proof is based on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts. In all previous applications of the $a$-contraction method to the study of long-time behavior, the proof has relied essentially on the parabolic structure provided by either viscosity or heat conduction. In this work, we extend the method to a hyperbolic-elliptic system without parabolic structure.

papers.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
papers.abstract: By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems. We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

papers.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
papers.abstract: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest. The stronger factorial normalization $((m-j)!i_j)_{j=0}^m$ is strictly log-concave; we give explicit coefficient margins, terminal sharpness, one-less smoothing, and the exact universal three-index binomial ULC prefix. An exact attachment argument doubles the rooted reserve for every nontrivial unweighted tree. For a single marked root, a square reserve holds through $Θ=\tfrac12e^{3-2W(1/e)}$ and for every positive mark at roots of degree at most four. A stronger reserve holds through mark $15/14$. These estimates yield marked clique, adjacent-pair, and repulsive two-piece variance bounds with fixed-weight canonical transfer. Finally, arbitrary positive site activities in $[3t/4,t]$ satisfy a uniform rooted reserve on every forest. This proves strict log-concavity for weighted forest coronas with compatible base marks. An explicit weighted-star obstruction shows why an unrestricted heterogeneous extension is impossible. Complete proofs are included, together with the required classical graph characterization and variance comparison.

papers.title: Local Budget Benefits, Population Commitment, and Solver Performance: A DGO Case Study with Controlled DE Transfer
papers.abstract: An evaluated candidate can improve a local search step, alter the population used by later steps, and affect a solver's final result. We distinguish these three questions using Da Gou Gun Optimization (DGO), a population optimizer designed for this study. Its JQ100 configuration evaluates an interpolation candidate during a two-sided probe. We define local budget value, population commitment effects and complete-policy performance, and give an exact example in which a locally better commitment leads to a worse continuation. Short-horizon matched comparisons favor interpolation on eligible quadratic states. Paired continuations yield mixed effect estimates, with primary group intervals spanning zero. Complete-policy comparisons favor JQ100 over the tested classical references in aggregate; a matched-start comparison has favorable means but intervals spanning parity. On 24 boxed BBOB functions, target-truncated geometric-mean error ratios favor JQ100 over the tested classical policies and favor L-SHADE and CMA-ES over JQ100 under the stated initialization and stopping rules. Local evaluation gains, commitment effects and solver competitiveness therefore require separate comparisons.

papers.title: Unavoidable flats in matroids excluding a uniform minor
papers.abstract: We extend a theorem of Geelen, Kroeker, and Nelson on unavoidable flats in $\operatorname{GF}(q)$-representable matroids. For all integers $1\le a\le b$ and $n\ge1$, we prove that every simple matroid of sufficiently large rank with no $U_{a,b}$-minor has a rank-$n$ flat whose restriction is free or isomorphic to a projective or affine geometry over a finite field.

papers.title: Robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems
papers.abstract: We develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed the robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz method (REMs-HS), for the efficient solution of high-frequency Helmholtz problems. The method combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver in a multiplicative way. A key ingredient of our construction is a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC), which is imposed both on the subdomain problems and on the local problems that generate the EMs coarse space. Compared with the original impedance boundary condition, the mIBC makes the proposed method both stable and inexpensive theoretically. We prove that the resulting REMs-HS preconditioner gives rise to a uniform convergent fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers. Moreover, the required resolution conditions are substantially relaxed. Only a mild condition on the level parameter $\ell$ of the hierarchical coarse basis $\ell>\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$ is needed, which is markedly weaker than the conditions in previous analyses. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.

papers.title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe2
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03504-zPrior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

papers.title: The challenge of recognition in large scientific collaborations
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03511-0The authorship practices of large collaborations can hide individual contributions. A recognition programme developed by the LIGO Scientific Collaboration publicly documents verified contributions to research, infrastructure and community service.

papers.title: Multiparticle quantum walks in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03512-zStrong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

papers.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $Δ_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations. When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.

papers.title: Stochastic Linesearch Methods for Stochastic Variational Inequality Problems: Parameter-Free Schemes and Non-Monotone Variants
papers.abstract: Much of the existing convergence guarantees and rate statements for stochastic variational inequality (SVI) problems are limited to stochastic approximation schemes that employ constant or diminishing steplength sequences bounded by some reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant $L$ of the map. This requires both knowing such constants and may lead to debilitatingly small steplengths, afflicting the scheme with potentially poor performance. We propose a parameter-free stochastic extragradient method with periodically restarted linesearch (\textbf{SEG-LS}) for solving pseudomonotone and monotone SVI problems. The resulting stepsize sequence is neither monotone nor requires prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant $L$. We show that the iteration and sample complexities for computing a point whose residual has norm at most $ε$ in expectation are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. These results improve to $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-1})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ in the monotone setting. In addition, we propose a periodically restarted biased stochastic linesearch method (\textbf{B-SLAM}) for solving non-monotone SVIs under strict copositivity. The resulting iteration and sample complexities are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. Preliminary numerics support these findings and display promise.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $φ$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $φ^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $φ^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $φ$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the Lévy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: String-averaging bargaining in solidarity cooperative games
papers.abstract: We consider the situation that the grand set of all players, in a cooperative game in characteristic function form with a nonempty core, consists of recognizable subsets of players. The underlying assumption is that the players of each subset have something in common between themselves which is not shared by the players of other subsets. For example, the members of these subsets are distinguishable by their nationalities or by their geographic locations or by some other market-related economic or social property. In addition to the agreement of all players to play the game to reach a point in the core, the members of each subset want to steer the iterative orbit of the bargaining process to a point in the core that will reflect the strength of their solidarity within their subset. This is why we call such subsets solidarity sets. The solidarity means that players of a solidarity set are willing to participate in coalitions that include only members of their solidarity set and are not willing to participate in coalitions of other solidarity sets. The question is how can such a game be played? Is there an iterative bargaining scheme that will generate a sequence of payoffs that converges to a point in the core which reflects the solidarity of the members of the solidarity sets? We propose bargaining schemes that allow the members of each solidarity set to perform, independently from other solidarity sets and, therefore, simultaneously in time, a full but finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration. Then the end-points of all these sweeps are combined into a single payoff vector via a convex combination wherein the coefficients of the convex combination may reflect some a priori knowledge about the relative strengths of the different solidarity sets. These bargaining schemes are applied to a new type of cooperative game that we call solidarity cooperative game (SCG).

papers.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
papers.abstract: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $β$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$. The goal of this paper is a bound of the form $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ that holds for every $t$, with $β$ small. We prove that, for every integer $t\geqslant2$, every graph with density at least $4.5\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor.

papers.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

papers.title: Box-Cone Representations of Bound-Factor RLT Constraints in Semidefinite Relaxations
papers.abstract: Linear inequalities can generate large constraint systems in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs, making the quadratic subproblems of splitting methods expensive to solve. We develop a box-cone representation of bound-factor reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) constraints in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs. These constraints arise by multiplying each original linear inequality by every binary variable and its complement and linearizing the resulting products. Our key observation is that all products generated by one inequality share a common slack and admit an exact representation in the standard cone over the unit box. This box-cone representation processes the inequalities through independent explicit projections, without introducing a separate nonnegative slack for each scalar RLT inequality. We illustrate the computational use of the representation within standard two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The resulting subproblems require linear solves with a reusable factorization and explicit cone projections, without enlarging the semidefinite matrix. Experiments on 257 binary quadratic programs compare this implementation with SDPNAL+. A second application groups Max-Cut triangle inequalities into box cones and uses the resulting bounds within an existing branch-and-bound framework. Tests on 220 graphs show competitive performance with MADAM using only triangle cuts. Together, these applications illustrate the representation's usefulness as a building block for first-order methods.

papers.title: On kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernel
papers.abstract: We prove the weak maximum principle and the Cucker-Smale flocking theorem for a general class of kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernels. This includes the classical Cucker-Smale and Motsch-Tadmor systems with defining kernel $φ$ assumed to be merely continuous or even $φ\in L^\infty$ for solutions in the Lebesgue class $f\in L^1$. For such models the characteristic flow-map is not well-defined and therefore the classical approaches of Cucker-Smale \cite{CS2007a,CS2007b} or Ha-Liu-Tadmor \cite{HL2009,HT2008} break down. We develop a new method adopted to rough settings based on Ambrossio's probabilistic representation of solutions and construction of dynamic barriers. All proofs are performed in the framework of so called bounded communication protocols, a non-smooth variant of regular protocols introduced in \cite{Shv-CPAM, Shv-EA} and representing a broad range of models of collective dynamics.

papers.title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs). In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts. Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

papers.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
papers.abstract: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $α^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $α$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

papers.title: Vacuum amplification across a programmable bosonic Bogoliubov stability boundary in a trapped-ion chain
papers.abstract: A quantum oscillator always carries vacuum fluctuations, and modulating its parameters converts them into correlated pairs of real quanta. This vacuum amplification underlies squeezed light and Hawking radiation. In a closed quadratic system, pair creation competes with the energy splitting of the modes, and growth turns exponential only once pairing overcomes the splitting. Here we realize this competition in two motional modes of a trapped-ion chain. A two-mode-squeezing drive creates the pairs, and a beam-splitter coupling splits the motion into two coupled modes at different frequencies. The two rates are tuned and calibrated independently. Starting near the motional ground state, we cross the stability boundary in two ways. First, with the drive at the sum of the two bare-mode frequencies, the phonon number stays bounded until the pairing rate exceeds the splitting and grows exponentially beyond it. Second, tuning the drive into resonance with one coupled mode lowers the threshold to zero, and only that mode is amplified into a squeezed vacuum. Separate control of the two interactions makes the threshold for vacuum amplification programmable. This control can be used to simulate particle creation and quantum phase transitions, and to operate parametrically driven bosonic devices close to their stability limit.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $κ$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tildeΔ$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--Göttsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tildeΔ}^κ|$ of $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$.

papers.title: Erdős--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

papers.title: CuPIQP: A Batched and Differentiable QP Solver on GPUs for Robot Learning and Control
papers.abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are fundamental building blocks of many robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and model predictive control. Extending these methods to large-scale robot learning and control requires solving many QPs concurrently and, for end-to-end learning, differentiating through their solutions. Efficient batched optimization is therefore essential to bringing established model-based methods into GPU-based robotics pipelines. We present \textsc{cuPIQP}, a batched and differentiable QP solver on GPUs based on a proximal interior-point method, with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems. The solver exploits parallelism across independent QPs and their internal structure while preserving per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions. Benchmarks with up to 16384 QPs per batch demonstrate solve-time speedups of up to $18.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau} and $4.26\times$ over eight-core \textsc{PIQP}. In an end-to-end learning task, \textsc{cuPIQP} accelerates training by $4.6\times$ over \textsc{QPAX} and $7.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau}. By reducing the computational cost, \textsc{cuPIQP} provides efficient, reusable infrastructure for integrating model-based optimization into large-scale robot learning and control.

papers.title: Neural Network Methods in the 2BSDE Formalism for Solving the High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation with Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: A 2BSDE system is written down for a $(D+1)$-dimensional Black--Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) with the Leland transaction cost model which incorporates the sign of the curvature. The 2BSDE system takes input from the ``speed'' (derivative of the curvature). This system is solved using a single ResNet neural network which learns both the solution to the PDE as well as the degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. The network is used to learn the price of derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets for $D=10,100$ achieving a time-averaged RMSE of less than $0.1$ in each case.

papers.title: Preparation of a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, hosting topological order and fractionalized anyonic excitations. Their realization poses a demanding target for quantum simulation. Here, we realize a bosonic FCI on an IBM Nighthawk superconducting quantum processor using classically optimized variational circuits. We target a Laughlin-like state that is an exact zero-energy ground state of a long-range parent Hamiltonian on a torus, eliminating physical edges and providing a favorable geometry for accessing fractional quantum Hall physics in a small system. On a $4\times4$ qubit lattice, we prepare both the four-boson FCI ground state and a three-boson state hosting two quasiholes. Measurements of particle densities and correlations reproduce the characteristic structure of the target states, while reconstructed chiral magnetization currents resolve the circulating current pattern associated with the quasiholes. The preparation of these strongly correlated topological states with shallow circuits establishes a route toward the digital simulation and manipulation of fractionalized excitations, including measurements of topological invariants and anyonic braiding.

papers.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $φ$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,φ}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,φ}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.

papers.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.

papers.title: Conformal geodesics and gauged Killing-Yano forms in dimension four
papers.abstract: We study the relation between conformal geodesics and conformal Killing-Yano (CKY) 2-forms on anti-self-dual conformal manifolds of dimension 4. In the flat case, twistor quadrics determine self-dual CKY forms whose zero loci contain conformal geodesics. To extend this construction to curved manifolds, we consider self-dual 2-forms with values in a line bundle and satisfying the gauged CKY equation, coupled to connections with anti-self-dual curvature. In this way we provide a local ambient characterization of non-null conformal geodesics as zero curves of gauged CKY forms, with the curvature vanishing along these curves.

papers.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period. In this paper we will show that the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow is free. We use symplectic geometry to investigate the topology of the quotient of the unit tangent bundle T^1M/S^1 by the S^1 action that comes from the geodesic flow. We show that this quotient admits the structure of a smooth symplectic manifold and that this symplectic manifold is symplectomorphic to S^2 \times S^2 equipped with a split form. This will enable a computation involving the Euler class of the orbibundle T^1M\rightarrow T^1M/S^1 which will lead to a solution of Berger's conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds.

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $Λ_{s,μ}(α)/μ$ with respect to the energy level $μ$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify linear maps $φ$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} φ(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $φ(A)=MAN$ or $φ(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

papers.title: Steady conformally Kähler Ricci solitons with isoparametric potential
papers.abstract: We classify complete, non-compact, simply connected, irreducible four-dimensional steady gradient Ricci solitons that are globally conformally Kähler and have an isoparametric potential. The steady Ricci solitons are $U(2)$-invariant nuts on $\mathbb R^4$, including the Bryant and Cao solitons, and bolts on $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb R^2$ and on $\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathbb{CP}^1$. For each $m\ge3$ there is exactly one non-collapsed bolt. A key step, valid for Ricci solitons of every sign, is that away from the locally conformally flat case, the conformal factor is aligned with the potential function, which yields cohomogeneity-one symmetry.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Variational Programs with Open Clocks
papers.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms leave the durations of Hamiltonian evolutions open for a classical optimizer to set. We present VHamilton, a minimal extension of the Hamilton quantum programming language in which such durations are open clocks: one program denotes a family of Hamiltonian trajectories, and a valuation fills its clocks with exact dyadic times, so that each instance is an ordinary Hamilton program that compiles to circuits as before. Because the semantics stays exact and affine in the clocks, the Hamiltonian structure of a variational program remainsavail able for reasoning about every valuation at once. Equivalence becomes a finite calculation, which we mechanize in Agda for a fragment and use to prove the VHamilton form of the compiler rewrite "rzz(t) = cx; rz(t); cx" for every clock value. We then show what the same structure supports in a two-qubit chemistry eigensolver written in VHamilton and run through a Haskell prototype. It supports a fusion of commuting blocks, a closed form and an expressibility proof for the ansatz, and an exact split of the error between the precision of the target and that of the clocks, with a priori bounds. It also supports a coordinate search whose queries per sweep, fixed by the spectra of the generators, do not grow with the precision. On the benchmark this search reaches the numerically verified optimum of a grid of 134 million valuations in 53 energy queries. It finds the grid optimum in only 21 of 30 validation settings, however, so the gain is conditional, not a global-optimization guarantee.

papers.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
papers.abstract: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.

papers.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: A nonlinear dynamical system can be characterized by the autonomous evolution of its state in time and its dependence on system parameters. As a parameter varies, the dynamics can change quantitatively and, at bifurcation points, qualitatively. When the governing equations are unknown, a data-driven model should therefore capture both elements from observational data, rather than reproduce the dynamics at a single operating condition only. Parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) is a model-free framework for this purpose, where the parameter is supplied to a reservoir computer through an additional input channel. PARC is trained on time series recorded at several parameter values, and the trained reservoir, run in closed loop as an autonomous dynamical system, generates trajectories at parameter values that were never observed. rc_prediction is an open-source Python package that implements this workflow. It provides multi-parameter training of a reservoir, autonomous closed-loop prediction at user-specified parameter values, parameter scans, and a standard echo state network for forecasting at a fixed parameter. Hyperparameter optimization and optional GPU acceleration through PyTorch are also provided. We use three benchmark dynamical systems as examples to demonstrate its usage.
